edges.description: Reduced HMGCL activity limits cleavage of HMG-CoA to acetoacetate and acetyl-CoA in hepatic ketogenesis.
The same enzyme defect blocks the final HMG-CoA cleavage step in leucine degradation.
Impaired HMG-CoA cleavage lowers acetoacetate and downstream ketone-body availability during catabolic stress.
Inadequate alternative fuel availability contributes to hypoketotic decompensation during fasting or illness.
intermediate_mechanisms: Catabolic stress increases reliance on hepatic ketogenesis while glucose intake and stores are limited.

edges.description: The model provides a candidate mechanism for hypoglycemia and secondary hyperammonemia during crisis.

edges.description: The convergent hypoketotic-hypoglycemia-plus-hepatic-dysfunction crisis produces the acute encephalopathic-hepatic attacks recognized clinically as Reye-syndrome-like episodes.

intermediate_mechanisms: Hypoglycemia, acidosis, and metabolic intoxication can injure the developing brain during severe crises.
